basic.definition: Row count, dimensionality and element type of the split.

invalid_values.definition: NaN and infinite coordinates (IEEE-754 bit patterns). Rows containing any are excluded from norm and distance metrics.

norms.definition: L2 norm of every row with finite values.

dimensions.definition: Per-dimension moments over finite values (population std; skewness g1; excess kurtosis g2 - 3).

sparsity.definition: Exact zeros among finite coordinates and non-zeros per valid row.

outliers_6_sigma.definition: Coordinates with |x - mean_d| > 6 * std_d of their dimension.

duplicates.definition: Rows with identical canonical values (-0.0 == 0.0, one NaN), grouped by a 128-bit hash; the false-positive probability is about N^2 / 2^129.

pairwise_distances.definition: Distances between uniformly drawn pairs of distinct sampled rows; metric distance uses the VSAG convention, geometric distance is Euclidean (chord for cosine).

sample.method: uniform without replacement (Floyd), seeded shuffle prefix

anisotropy.definition: Directional concentration: mean pairwise cosine similarity (sample), mean-vector norm over the average row norm (full).

nearest_neighbors.definition: Exact k nearest neighbors of sampled query rows searched in the full split (the query row itself excluded), VSAG metric convention.

sample.method: uniform without replacement (Floyd), seeded shuffle prefix

nearest_neighbors.isolated_definition: First-neighbor geometric distance above the Tukey far-out fence of all queries.

intrinsic_dimensionality.definition: Local intrinsic dimensionality: Levina-Bickel MLE from the k geometric neighbor distances of each query; TwoNN (Facco et al.) from first/second neighbor ratios.

sample.method: uniform without replacement (Floyd), seeded shuffle prefix

intrinsic_dimensionality.two_nn_excluded_definition: Queries whose first neighbor is a duplicate or ties the second neighbor; TwoNN skips them.

relative_contrast.definition: Per query: mean geometric distance to reference sampled rows divided by the first-neighbor distance. Lower values mean harder nearest-neighbor search.

sample.method: uniform without replacement (Floyd), seeded shuffle prefix

hubness.definition: k-occurrence N_k: how often each sampled row appears in the k-NN lists of the other sampled rows (Radovanovic et al., JMLR 2010). Skewness > 1 indicates hubs.

sample.method: uniform without replacement (Floyd), seeded shuffle prefix

pca.definition: Eigenvalues of the sample covariance (n - 1 denominator). Effective rank is exp(entropy of the normalized spectrum); participation ratio is (sum lambda)^2 / sum lambda^2.

sample.method: uniform without replacement (Floyd), seeded shuffle prefix

clustering.definition: k-means (k-means++ seeding, Lloyd iterations) on sampled rows; balance and separation summarize coarse partition structure, e.g. for IVF bucket balance.

sample.method: uniform without replacement (Floyd), seeded shuffle prefix

projection.definition: Sampled rows projected on the two leading principal axes; the third value is the k-means cluster.

sample.method: uniform without replacement (Floyd), seeded shuffle prefix

quantization.definition: Recall@k of simulated VSAG quantizers (ranges and floor encoding as in ScalarQuantizationTrainer) against exact search on a sampled base. A model, not a benchmark: confirm with eval_performance.

sample.method: uniform without replacement (Floyd), seeded shuffle prefix
sample.subset: first quantization_base valid sampled train rows
